text: Your heart just stopped. Here's what happens to your body.
In seconds, blood stops moving, your brain runs out of oxygen, and you collapse.
You might gasp for air, but that's not real breathing.
After about five minutes without oxygen, your brain starts to get damaged.
After eight to ten minutes, your chance of surviving drops fast.
But someone near you can keep you alive.
They push hard and fast in the middle of your chest, at least two inches deep, over a hundred times a minute.
That keeps blood flowing to your brain until an AED can shock your heart to restart it.
Fast CPR can double or triple your chance of living. And most of the time, this happens at home.
And that's what happens when your heart stops.
